description.narrative: The International Development Law Organisation (IDLO) har inkommit med en ansökan om 30 MSEK för att stödja ett projekt med syfte att öka de kenyanska medborgarnas tillgång till rättssystemet/rättvisa, öka transparens och ansvarsutkrävande på både nationell och länsnivå, enligt Kenyas grundlag från 2010. Insatsen kommer att stödja nyckelinstitutioner inom rättsväsendet för att genomföra den strategiska planen och styrdokumentet "Sustaining Judiciary Transformation" (SJT). Projektet kommer även att stödja det 'nationella rådet för rättsskipning' (National Council on Administration of Justice, NCAJ), där bl.a. aktörer inom straffrätten ingår, i dess reformer mot större öppenhet och ansvarsutkrävande från medborgarna. Rättshjälp (legal aid) är en annan viktig komponent i projektet som kommer stödja implementeringen av den lag från 2016 som ska säkra att även utsatta människor får tillgång till rättshjälp. Projektet kommer även att arbeta med civilsamhällesorganisationer och grundlagskommissioner vad gäller öppenhet och ansvarsutkrävande, inklusive mekanismer för allmänheten att framföra klagomål mot nationella och lokala myndigheter. Viktiga aktörer som den kenyanska riksrevisionen, antikorruptionskommissionen, justitiedepartementet, guvernörsrådet (Council of Governors), finansdepartementet och parlamentets budgetkontor kommer att stödjas i arbetet med att ta fram policydokument och efterlevnad

The International Development Law Organisation (IDLO) has submitted a proposal of 30 MSEK to support a project aiming to increase access to justice for the Kenyan citizens, increase transparency and accountability on national and county levels, in line with the 2010 Constitution of Kenya. The contribution will support key institutions within the justice sector to implement their Strategic Plan as well as the blueprint " Sustaining Judiciary Transformation" (SJT). The project will also support the National Council on Administration of Justice (NCAJ), including actors within the criminal justic chain, with the ongoing implementation of reforms. Legal aid is another substantial component in the project, and the implementation of the 2016 Legal Aid Act aiming to secure legal aid to vulnerable people, will receive support. The project will also support CSOs and Constitutional Commissions in terms of transparency and accountability, including public complaints handling mechanisms. Important actors such as the Office of the Auditor General; Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission, the OAG/DOJ, the Council of Governors, the National Treasury and the Parliamentary Budget Office will be supported in developing of policies and compliance.
The project aims to enhancing access to justice, transparency and accountability at both county and national levels in Kenya, in line with the 2010 Constitution of Kenya.

1. IDLO supported the enhancement of access to justice through reduction of case backlog: The programme target was to increase by 5% the no of cases filed and concluded through Court Annexed Mediation (CAM). The programme achieved an increase of 236% from 2018-2022. Specifically, CAM recorded a 62% conclusion rate for matters referred to CAM and a 33% settlement rate for cases where parties reached settlement agreements in 50 courts where CAM was implemented. Statistics in the State of the Judiciary and Administration of Justice Reports (SOJAR) showed significant progress in dealing with case backlog at the Court of Appeal (COA) and the High Court where Court Annexed Mediation (CAM) was implemented. Between the 2017/2018 and 2020/20212 Financial Years (FYs), the Judiciary recorded a Avslutspromemoria Completion Memo Contribution ID: 11341 2 (8) 24.4 % increase in the number of cases filed and a 3% increase in the number of cases concluded overall. IDLO contributed to this progress through initiatives such as implementation of Court of Appeal (COA) service weeks in Mombasa, and Kisumu in 2019 and 2020. This was also achieved through implementation of children court service weeks to accelerate the resolution of children matters that would otherwise remain in court; and the roll-out and implementation of CAM in additional 36 magistrate courts. 2. IDLO supported the expanded access to justice through Court Annexed Mediation (CAM): At the beginning of the project in September 2018, CAM was operational in 14 court stations limited to Nairobi only. By June 2021, CAM had been operationalized in 50 court stations across the country (16 High Court, 5 Environment and Labour Relations, 5 Environment and Land and 24 Magistrates Courts). Following the adoption of the CAM Action Plan (2021-2024) in 2021 with support from IDLO, the Judiciary allocated 29 million KES and 50 million KES to pay CAM mediators, compared to the previous allocation of Kenya Shillings 32 million in the previous FY. The increase in the allocation of Government funding to support CAM has enhanced the sustainability of CAM beyond the lifetime of the project and strengthened ownership of CAM by the Government. CAM presented one of the best models for improving access to justice through Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), especially for the vulnerable and marginalized, as it is offered at no cost for the litigants; is faster than litigation; and focused on maintaining/restoring relations. 3. Enhanced access to justice through the development and adoption of quality rules and regulations: IDLO supported the development of 12 policy and operational procedures. The following were adopted and are currently in use: - the Small Claims Court (SCC) Rules, Civil Procedure (Amendment) Rules, Access to Information Regulations. Technical support by IDLO ensured the finalization of the Quality Control Guidelines for the Development of Effective Legislative Proposals, which is currently used by the Rules Committee of the Judiciary (RCJ) to develop subsidiary legislation. 4. Enabling environment for enhanced access to justice for women and children created: IDLO supported the improvement of the policy frameworks on access to justice for children through technical support for the development of (i) the Diversion Toolkit for Children in Kenya; (ii) Standards Operational Procedures (SOPs) for Police Child Protection Units; (iii) the Childrens Courts Practice Directions; (iv) a Training Curriculum for juvenile justice actors; and (v) the Protocol on Service Weeks for Childrens matters. These policy frameworks clarify legal positions and make it easier for children to access justice. The development of similar frameworks on gender justice, through a combination of capacity development and technical support, also enhanced the capacity of judicial officers in the administration of gender justice and encouraged gender-responsive adjudication of matters. Improved quality of legal aid services: IDLO supported the development of three (3) operational documents for the National Legal Aid Services (NLAS)including the NLAS Strategic Plan (2021- 2025), NLAS Status Report (2016- 2021), and the NLAS handbook on FAQ's). The handbook are currently used as sources of information by clients who represent themselves in court because they cannot afford legal representation. To ensure continuity of access to informed legal aid services during the COVID-19 pandemic, IDLO supported capacity development for legal aid service providers in Nyeri, Meru, and Turkana, to increase understanding and effective application of the Legal Aid Act. IDLO supported the NLAS to organize and deliver trainings for 178 (F: 72; M: 106) legal aid service providers, host five (5) radio talk shows on access to legal aid services during the COVID-19 pandemic and to meet the increased demand for accessible legal aid services in the communities. The use of radio platforms facilitated outreach to farflung communities who lack information on access to legal aid and are unable to access NLAS offices. IDLO supported the National police service (NPS)to organize and deliver trainings for 43 (F: 15; M: 28) senior superintendents and county commanders in Kisumu County and Makueni on access to justice for women and children. The training sessions equipped NPS leaders with knowledge of the obligations of the NPS in the prevention and response to gender-based violence (GBV) and effective management of GBV cases to support prosecution. 6. Knowledge products on anti-corruption and oversight of public institutions developed: IDLO supported the development of (i) the Case Digest on Anti-Corruption and Economic Crimes; (ii) the Case Digest of the Public Procurement Administrative Review Board (PPARB) decisions; and (iii) the Compendium of Cases on Devolution. The Case Digests and Compendium of Cases serve as reference tools for judicial officers, litigants, and other stakeholders in their interaction with adjudication of cases on anti-corruption, public procurement, and devolution. To strengthen transparency and accountability, the following were undertaken with the support of the project i)monitoring State compliance to international and regional obligations under the United Nations Convention Against Corruption (UNCAC) and the African Union Convention on Preventing and Combating Corruption (AUCPCC); (ii) supporting convenings and platforms for dialogues with stakeholders on the anti-corruption agenda; and (iii) publication of information materials that facilitate the performance of the oversight roles. This included OAGs first and second cycle review reports under UNCAC; the National Anti Corruption Campaign Steering Committees (NACCST) IEC materials on anti-corruption; (iii) the report of the Task Force on the comprehensive review of the legal, policy and institutional framework on fighting corruption; (iv) the End of Term Report of the Commissioner of the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR); (v) KNCHRs Kenya @10: A Avslutspromemoria Completion Memo Contribution ID: 11341 4 (8) Decade After Report; and (vi) Kenya Law Reform Commission (KLRC) 2018 Annual Report. 7. Technical assistance to key constitutional commissions and independent offices with transparency and accountability mandates IDLO provided technical support to the Council of Gvernors (COG) to carry out a legal audit on the devolved functions under Schedule four of the Constitution and develop the legal audit report. The findings of the legal audit report informed policy, legislative and administrative reforms on devolution. IDLO also supported the development and launch of an implementation framework for the audit report to address gaps identified in the legal audit and strengthen the satisfaction of devolved functions. IDLO supported the Kenya Judiciary Academy (KJA) to organize and deliver a workshop for 30 (F: 8; M: 22) judges on emerging jurisprudence on devolution in October 2021. The workshop, a first for KJA, provided a platform for the judges to reflect on their roles as judicial officers in the adjudication of devolution matters and enhancing access to justice on devolution. 8. Gender Mainstreaming.- A gender analysis of the programme was conducted in 2018, which informed the integration of some gender-mainstreamed activities across the outcomes as well as the implementation of gender-specific activities. The activities promoted the principles of gender equality, nondiscrimination, and inclusion of vulnerable groups such as women and children. A notable achievement was the report on the Status of Intersex Persons in the Criminal Justice System in Kenya that provided updated data on intersex persons within the criminal justice system, to inform planning to address their unique vulnerabilities and ensure that their right to dignified treatment is respected.
